title: Constructibility from the cardinalities of finite stalks
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian
scheme and let $F$ be an
abelian etale sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]
with finite geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].
For $n\geq1$ put $C_n=\{x\in X:|F_{\bar x}|=n\}$.
Then $F$ is constructible
if and only if every $C_n$ is a constructible subset of $X$ [def-weil-constructible-subset].
For an abelian sheaf, constructibility here means a finite locally
closed partition with finite locally constant restrictions.

external.place: The classical statement is [SGA 4, Exposition IX, Proposition 2.13(iii)](https://grothendiecksga.com/read/sga4/en/IX-2.html).

proof.text: Suppose F is constructible in the abelian sense [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf]. Fix one of its finitely many locally closed strata S. On an etale trivializing cover V_i of S the restriction is the constant abelian sheaf with finite value A_i. The inverse-image stalk isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] and the constant stalk theorem [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] identify its stalks with A_i. Every geometric point over a point of the image of V_i lifts to V_i [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift], so cardinality equals |A_i| on that entire image. Etale morphisms are flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism], so these images are open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. For each n their union with |A_i|=n is C_n intersect S, and the union with |A_i| unequal to n is its complement in S. Hence C_n intersect S is clopen in S, thus locally closed in X. There are only finitely many strata; their union is constructible by the Noetherian characterization in [def-weil-constructible-subset]. This does not presume a finite etale cover or globally constant cardinality on a stratum.

source.place: Proposition 2.13(iii), forward implication; abelian group version of 2.4

proof.text: For the converse perform Noetherian induction on the closed subsets T of X, giving each its reduced induced closed subscheme structure supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. On an affine Noetherian chart Spec(R) of X this structure is Spec(R/I); any ascending chain of ideals of R/I lifts to an ascending chain of ideals of R containing I, so R/I is Noetherian. Its underlying closed subset is quasi-compact, hence this is a Noetherian scheme. The induction assertion is that the abelian inverse image F_T has a finite locally closed partition with finite locally constant abelian restrictions. The empty closed subset has the empty partition. At T assume the assertion for every proper closed subset. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] the stalks of F_T are those of F at the corresponding geometric points, so they are finite, and its cardinality level sets are C_n intersect T. These are constructible in T by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], the closed subsets of X satisfy the minimal condition, giving the stated Noetherian induction. A chain of subsets closed in a fixed closed T is also a chain of closed subsets of X, so the same condition holds in T. It therefore suffices to construct one nonempty open W of a nonempty T where F_T is finite locally constant; its complement is proper closed, to which the induction hypothesis applies. In the next steps write X and F for T and F_T.

source.place: Proposition 2.13(iii), final Noetherian induction; blueprint paragraph 2; reduced closed structure: Stacks 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), 01J4 (definition-reduced-induced-scheme), schemes.tex; scheme-to-topology passage: Stacks 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology), properties.tex, and 0051 (definition-noetherian), topology.tex

proof.text: Choose an irreducible component of the nonempty X and its generic point eta, whose existence is supplied by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. There are finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. Remove all components other than the chosen one. The resulting open X_0 contains eta and is irreducible. Let M=F_bar_eta and m=|M|, which is at least 1 for an abelian group. The constructible set C_m intersect X_0 is a finite union of locally closed subsets [def-weil-constructible-subset] and contains eta. One of those subsets contains eta. In an expression O intersect Z for that subset, Z is closed in X_0 and contains eta, so Z=X_0. Thus it contains a nonempty open U of X_0 on which every stalk has exactly m elements.

source.place: Proposition 2.13(iii), reduction to constant cardinality; blueprint paragraph 2

proof.text: The stalk is the colimit of sections on pointed etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Its index is filtered by [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]; use a small skeleton of affine pointed objects, with all their lifts, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover]. Affine open refinement retains the marked point, so this subsystem is cofinal for stalks. Apply the elementwise filtered-colimit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] with R=Z (abelian groups are Z-modules) to lift every a in the finite group M to a section s_a on a common pointed etale neighbourhood V_0 of bar_eta in U. Each of the finitely many relations s_0=0 and s_a+s_b=s_(a+b) has zero germ. The same theorem kills each relation after a further refinement, and cofilteredness gives one common pointed refinement on which all hold. The table a maps to s_a is now a group homomorphism M to F(V_0). Restricting these sections to each etale object over V_0 gives a natural map from the constant abelian presheaf to F restricted to V_0. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] it extends uniquely to phi:constant M to F restricted to V_0. Restriction and inverse image agree by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. The constant stalk theorem identifies its marked stalk map with the identity of M.

source.place: Proposition 2.13(i), finite-fibre section lifting with group operations; blueprint paragraph 3

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-generic-irreducible-neighbourhood] to V_0 to U and the underlying point of its marked lift over eta. Here U is Noetherian and irreducible, eta is its component generic point, and V_0 to U is etale; no reducedness or normality is assumed. It gives an irreducible open V retaining the marked lift whose underlying point is generic in V. Restrict each section s_a to V. Restriction is a homomorphism, so s_0=0 and s_a+s_b=s_(a+b) still hold. For each etale object E over V, send a to s_a restricted to E; these homomorphisms commute with restriction and define a morphism from the constant abelian presheaf with value M to F restricted to V. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends this to phi:constant M to F restricted to V, with the source defined by [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The restriction sheaf agrees with abelian inverse image by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. Germ compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies the retained germs of these sections with their original germs, namely a; [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] identifies the source stalk with M through these same constant sections. Hence the newly defined phi induces the identity on M at the retained point.

source.place: Proposition 2.13(ii), irreducible etale generic neighbourhood; blueprint paragraph 3

proof.text: For a nonzero a in M let Z_a be the set of points of V where the section phi(a)=s_a has zero geometric germ. The elementwise stalk-colimit criterion [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], with the pointed neighbourhood and smallness results of step 4, says that a zero germ vanishes as a section on a further pointed etale neighbourhood. Conversely vanishing as a section gives zero germs throughout that neighbourhood; the germ identification [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] makes this assertion independent of restriction notation. Its image in V is open by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], and geometric points over every point of that image lift by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift]. Thus Z_a is precisely a union of open images. It omits the generic point: if any vanishing neighbourhood had that point in its image, the retained geometric generic point would lift to that neighbourhood by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift], forcing s_a to have zero germ at the retained lift, contrary to the identity marked stalk map. Thus no choice-independence theorem for germs is being assumed. Every nonempty open of irreducible V contains its generic point, so Z_a is empty. The constant stalk theorem [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] identifies every source stalk with M; consequently phi is injective on all stalks. The inverse-image stalk theorem identifies every target stalk with a stalk of F at a point of U, hence both source and target have m elements. An injective map of finite sets of the same cardinality is bijective. By [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], phi is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves on V.

source.place: Proposition 2.13(iii), generic fibre injectivity and equal cardinalities; blueprint paragraph 4

proof.text: The image W of V to X is a nonempty open by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. The same map V to W is an etale surjection and its restriction of F is constant with finite abelian value M by step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. This is the required finite locally constant condition in [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf]; the inverse-image composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] identifies the iterated restriction with the original one. The induction hypothesis of step 2 gives a finite lisse partition on X minus W. Regard those strata as strata of X through the closed immersion, and adjoin W. Locally closed subsets of a closed subset remain locally closed in X; by [def-weil-constructible-subset] they are constructible since X is Noetherian. The composition isomorphism identifies their abelian inverse images with the restrictions provided by induction. This proves the induction assertion and the converse. For empty X the empty partition already proves both directions. The obtained finite partition, with finitely many constant cardinalities on each Noetherian stratum after a finite subcover of the open trivializing images, also yields a finite image of the cardinality function; an infinite union of constructible sets was never used to infer a bound.
